title: Computation
definition: Computation is the rule-governed transformation of inputs and state into outputs or new state.
purpose: Give learners a technology-neutral model for reasoning about what execution accomplishes.
history: Models of computation formalize how rule-governed steps transform representations; this record uses only the introductory input-state-output boundary.
mental_model: Computation consumes an input and current state, applies defined rules, and produces output or changed state.
analogy: A controlled recipe transforms ingredients and kitchen state into a dish, but human improvisation makes the analogy less strict than machine computation.
real_world_usage: Separating observable output from internal state
common_mistakes: Ignoring state changes that are not printed
industry_notes: Clear input, state, and output boundaries support contracts, tests, and observability.
ai_notes: AI can propose a transformation, but execution and tests are needed to establish actual behavior.
interview_notes: Ask the candidate to identify input, state transition, and output in a simple process.
exercise_candidates: Annotate inputs, intermediate state, and outputs
lab_candidates: Trace a rule-governed transformation across several steps
project_candidates: Specify the state transition contract of a simulator
